title: A cylinder is a circle, stacked

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Volume measures space in cubic units. This box has nine unit cubes in one layer.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Stack two layers, then three. Nine times three is twenty-seven cubic units.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A cylinder works the same way. Only the layer's shape changes.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Start with a circle. Its radius, from center to edge, is five units.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Its area is pi times the radius times itself: twenty-five pi square units.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Give it a thickness of one unit. The disc holds twenty-five pi cubic units.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two layers: fifty pi.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three layers: seventy-five pi.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four layers: one hundred pi cubic units. Every unit of height adds the same amount.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: So volume is circle area times height. Even a fraction of a layer contributes that fraction of its volume.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Radius ten inches, height four inches. The circle's area is one hundred pi square inches.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four one-inch layers hold four hundred pi cubic inches. If the volume is *a* pi, *a* is four hundred.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Diameter twenty feet, height eight feet. Diameter goes all the way across the center.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The radius is half: ten feet. Square that center-to-edge distance.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The circle's area is one hundred pi. Eight layers give eight hundred pi cubic feet.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: What if the volume is five hundred pi cubic inches, and the radius is five inches? Find the height.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Pull out one one-inch layer. It holds twenty-five pi cubic inches. How many of those make five hundred pi?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Divide total volume by one layer's volume. Five hundred divided by twenty-five is twenty layers: twenty inches tall.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Radius three meters, height fourteen meters. Nine pi per one-meter layer, times fourteen, gives one hundred twenty-six pi cubic meters.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Keeping pi gives the exact volume. Use three point one four for pi when the problem asks for that estimate.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One hundred twenty-six times three point one four is three hundred ninety-five point six four cubic meters, approximately.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Pi times radius squared is the circle's area. Height counts how many unit-thick layers fill the cylinder.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A cylinder's volume is its circle, stacked as high as it goes.
